title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Claude Code's July update pushes agent autonomy deeper into the harness — background agents self-commit, subagents inherit model + thinking config
bullets.summary: Background agents now commit, push, and open a draft PR when they finish instead of asking; the Explore agent inherits the session model (capped at opus) instead of haiku; subagents and compaction inherit extended-thinking config; and a new /dataviz skill ships with a color-palette validator.
bullets.how: These are exactly the harness patterns The Construct hand-built (Hermes commit/push, model-tiered subagents, higher-quality scans); adopt the native auto-commit/draft-PR flow where safe and let subagents inherit thinking to lift scan quality without extra plumbing.

bullets.title: Claude gains Microsoft 365 write tools — draft/send email, manage calendars, create and update OneDrive & SharePoint files
bullets.summary: Claude moves from reading M365 to acting in it, closing the loop on office workflows.
bullets.how: A ready-made write surface for PRAGMA client ops and Construct back-office automation on Microsoft-shop accounts; scope which client workflows (proposals, calendars, doc updates) we hand to it vs. keep in our own tools.

bullets.title: Bespoke Labs raises $40M Series A to build environments where agents safely learn, test, and improve before production
bullets.summary: Rather than another foundation model, the company builds simulation + evaluation infrastructure so agents get reliable through large-scale testing (Wing VC, Mayfield).
bullets.how: A funded bet on the exact layer that is The Construct's durable moat (verification loops, eval before deploy); validates investing our own build in test/eval harnesses, and worth tracking as a possible buy for agent QA.

bullets.title: Taktile lands $110M Series C for an agentic decision platform with human oversight and audit trails
bullets.summary: Automates loan approvals, fraud triage, claims and onboarding for banks/insurers while preserving human-in-the-loop and auditability (led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives).
bullets.how: A proof point for PRAGMA's AI-operator thesis in regulated verticals: the winning pattern is automation + explicit human checkpoints + audit logs, not full autonomy; mirror that design in client-facing operator builds.

bullets.title: Model routing stays in flux — Gemini 3.5 Pro delayed to July 17 (2M context, 'Deep Think'), GPT-5.6 broad access expected mid-July
bullets.summary: Two frontier options for reasoning/coding-heavy and long-document work land inside the same window.
bullets.how: Keep our model-routing layer provider-agnostic; benchmark both against Sonnet 5 when they ship and reserve 2M-context calls for long-document Construct jobs, but don't re-architect around unreleased models.

praxis_lesson: The platform keeps swallowing harness plumbing — this week it's background agents that commit/push/open their own PRs and subagents that inherit model and thinking config, the exact scaffolding we wrote by hand. Meanwhile fresh capital (Bespoke's $40M for agent test/eval environments, Taktile's $110M for auditable human-in-the-loop automation) is flowing one layer up, into verification and governed autonomy. Retire our custom plumbing for the native flow, and concentrate build where the money and the moat now sit — the eval/verification loop and domain-specific human-checkpoint design nothing commoditizes for us.
